curriculum.lesson_evidence: Seasons are yearly patterns of weather and day length. A useful Stage 2 model links seasons to Earth’s yearly path and tilt (keep language age-right: tilt means parts of Earth lean toward/away from Sun across the year).
curriculum.scope_limit: Single lesson: partial evidence. Cross-check existing card mapping and NESA content point. Official wording for MA2-RN-01 is recorded in lesson-pipeline/sources/nesa-ma2-rn-01.json where applicable.

lesson.child_mission: Seasons are yearly patterns of weather and day length. A useful Stage 2 model links seasons to Earth’s yearly path and tilt (keep language age-right: tilt means parts of Earth lean toward/away from Sun across the year).
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same science idea to a new object or material, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Sort typical NSW: beach weather and long daylight; frost mornings and early dark — which seasons?

FEEDBACK
Summer-like; winter-like.

WATCH FOR
Thinking Earth is closer to the Sun in summer (only) is a common mix-up; tilt/day length ideas matter more in the school model.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Make a seasons poster for your place: typical weather, day length idea and two living-thing changes per season. State Australia/NSW context.

Write a short reflection naming one observation or step you corrected and why.
